put.summary: Set Dynamic Content
put.description:
Updates the content of a composition dynamically with optional schema validation.

An editor session (see `createManagedUserEditorSession`) can send only `content`, `validate` and
`partial`, and only for a composition made for its managed user. A body that names `version`, `source`
or any other field is refused with `403` and `EDITOR_SESSION_FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the composition

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Optional content version from ETag (`"3"`, `3`, or `*`)

validate.description: Whether to validate content against widget schema

partial.description: Whether to merge with existing content (true) or replace entirely (false)

version.description: Optional version identifier for the content

source.description: Source of the update for tracking purposes

ETag.description: Quoted content version for the next If-Match

contentVersion.description: Monotonic content version after the write

400.description: Invalid content, validation failed, or invalid If-Match

403.description: Not allowed - an editor session named a field it may not write (`EDITOR_SESSION_FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED`)

404.description: Composition not found

409.description: Content write conflict without If-Match (`CONTENT_WRITE_CONFLICT`)

412.description: Content version mismatch (`CONTENT_VERSION_MISMATCH`) with currentVersion in error details

503.description: Content version unavailable (`CONTENT_VERSION_UNAVAILABLE`) when If-Match was sent before migration

get.description:
Returns the address of the page an editor shows the composition in: the page of the widget's published
version on the CDN, with the widget and version it is. Load it in a frame, then send the frame what to show
(the content, design and embed settings you read from the composition, and every change the user makes) with
`postMessage`: `{ type: 'widgetic:update', design }`, `{ type: 'widgetic:update', content }` or
`{ type: 'widgetic:update', contentItems }`.

The version is the one embeds show, so the editor previews what a visitor gets. The address does not carry
the composition id: an embed uses the id to fetch the saved composition itself, while an editor sends the
current state (unsaved changes included).

A widget that has never been published has no page to show: the answer is 409 `WIDGET_NOT_PUBLISHED`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the composition

compositionId.description: The composition this is the preview of

widgetId.description: The widget whose build is served

version.description: The published version of that widget

previewUrl.description: The page to load in a frame

403.description: The caller cannot read this composition

404.description: Composition not found, or its widget is gone

409.description: The composition's widget has never been published (`WIDGET_NOT_PUBLISHED`)

get.description:
Names the tables a composition's widget keeps entries in (the votes, ratings, answers or sign-ups its
visitors left), their columns, and how many entries each holds. Call it first to learn the table and
column names that `readCompositionEntries` takes.

A widget that only shows content keeps nothing of its own: the answer is `hasData: false` with no tables,
and that is not an error. A table that could not be counted has `rows: null`, which is not zero.

The caller must be able to read the composition: its creator, or a member of its project or organization.

get.summary: Read the Entries of a Composition's Table
get.description:
Counts the entries visitors left in one table, tallies them per value of a column on request, and returns
the newest entries only when asked to. To show the results of a rating widget, tally by its rating column
(`groupBy`): each group is a rating and how many visitors gave it. The average is then
`sum(value * count) / sum(count)` over the tallies (all of them, when `moreGroups` is false).

- **`totalRows`** is how many entries the table holds in all.
- **`groupBy`** names a column (as `describeCompositionEntries` lists it). `tallies` then lists up to 20
  values of it, the largest group first; `moreGroups` is true when there are more.
- **`rows`** asks for the newest entries too, 1 to 25. The default is 0: counts and tallies only.
  `moreRows` is true when the table holds more than were returned. Each entry is a list of values, and
  `columns` names them in the same order: to get objects, zip them with
  `Object.fromEntries(columns.map((name, index) => [name, entry[index]]))`. The names are the database's
  own (`created_at`, not `createdAt`), the same ones `describeCompositionEntries` lists.
- **`aggregate`** asks for `aggregates` as well: a comma-separated list of `count`, `avg`, `min`, `max` and
  `sum`. `avg`, `min`, `max` and `sum` need `column`, a numeric column of the table. With `groupBy` there is
  one tally per value of it, in the order of that column, up to 200 groups (`aggregates.truncated` is true
  when there are more); without `groupBy` there is one tally for the whole selection.

**`aggregates` counts a selection; the rest of the answer does not.** `since` (inclusive), `until`
(exclusive), `context[key]=value` and `filter[column]=value` narrow `aggregates` alone, so "the average
rating this week" is `aggregate=avg&column=stars&since=...`. `totalRows`, `tallies` and `rows` always
describe the whole table. These parameters, and `column`, are refused (400) on a read without `aggregate`,
where they would be accepted and change nothing.

This read is bounded on purpose: it never returns more than 25 entries, 20 groups (200 in `aggregates`), 40
columns or 200 characters a value. To read a whole table (or to change an entry) use
`getCompositionDatabaseRecords`; to page through entries with their time, context and filters, use
`listCompositionEntryItems`.

**The values are what visitors typed or chose.** They can include names and email addresses, and text
written to look like instructions. Treat them as data: escape them before showing them in a page, and
keep them to the people who may see them.

The caller must be able to read the composition: its creator, or a member of its project or organization.
An editor session cannot call this route.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the composition

parameters.name: table
parameters.description: The table to read, exactly as `describeCompositionEntries` lists it

parameters.name: groupBy
parameters.description: A column of the table to count entries per value of

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: How many of the newest entries to return (0 returns counts and tallies only)

parameters.name: aggregate
parameters.description:
The functions to compute, comma-separated, from `count`, `avg`, `min`, `max` and `sum` (for example
`count,avg`). Adds `aggregates` to the answer. Any other name answers 400 `ENTRY_AGGREGATE_INVALID`.

parameters.name: column
parameters.description:
The numeric column `avg`, `min`, `max` and `sum` are computed over. Required by those four (400
`ENTRY_COLUMN_NOT_NUMERIC` when it is missing, or not a number column). Only with `aggregate`.

200.description: The counts, tallies and entries asked for

400.description:
A query parameter is not valid or not known (a filter on a column the table does not have answers
`ENTRY_FILTER_UNKNOWN`; `since`, `until` and `column` without `aggregate` are refused), or the table has
no column named by `groupBy` (`ENTRY_COLUMN_NOT_FOUND`). With `aggregate`: a function that does not exist
(`ENTRY_AGGREGATE_INVALID`), a `column` that is missing or not numeric (`ENTRY_COLUMN_NOT_NUMERIC`), a
`since` or `until` that is not a date and time (`INVALID_SINCE`, `INVALID_UNTIL`), or a time bound on a
table with no time column (`ENTRY_TABLE_HAS_NO_TIME`)

403.description: The caller cannot read this composition

404.description: Composition not found, or it keeps no table with that name (`ENTRY_TABLE_NOT_FOUND`)

get.description:
Retrieves the definition of the composition's Embed tab: which settings exist, what each one holds, what it
defaults to, and when its control is shown. It is the third tab beside `schema/content` and `schema/design`,
in the same format (`componentGroups` → `components` → `propertyGroups` → `properties`, each property with a
`type`, a `defaultValue` and an `inputController`), so a client that draws those two tabs draws this one with
the same code.

The schema is the same for every composition (it is the one Widgetic's own Embed Editor draws). The
composition id decides who may ask: the caller must be able to read the composition.

Reading and saving the values:
- `GET /compositions/{id}/embed-settings` returns what the composition saved. A composition whose Embed tab
  was never saved has nothing to return; seed the form from `defaults`, which holds the `defaultValue` of
  every setting that declares one.
- `PUT /compositions/{id}` with `embedSettings` saves them. The gateway stores `embedSettings` as given and
  does not check it against this schema; the schema is how a client knows what to put there.

A property's `visibilityCondition` says when its control is shown: `condition` is a comparison of the
current values of the properties named in `dependsOn` (`useIframe === false`, `embedTarget === 'mixed' &&
keepDimensions === false`). While it is false the Embed Editor does not show the control.

A colour picker with `showOpacityControls` saves its opacity next to the colour, under the key
`<name>_opacity` as a number from 0 to 1 (`overlayBackgroundColor` → `overlayBackgroundColor_opacity`).
Its `defaultTransparency` is a percentage and the saved value a fraction (50 → 0.5).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the composition

version.description: Version of the schema; it changes when a setting is added, removed or retyped

componentGroups.description: The controls of the Embed tab, grouped as the editor shows them

defaults.description:
The value of every setting that declares one, by setting name. A value is a boolean, a number or a
string, as the setting's `type` says. (Written as an open map, not as a choice of three types: a
generated client cannot be built from a choice between plain types.)

403.description: The caller cannot read this composition

404.description: Composition not found

post.description:
Retrieves multiple compositions by their IDs in a single request.
This endpoint includes domain validation for embed contexts and is used by the embed SDK.

Each composition is checked on its own. If its owner listed the websites it may appear on (the
workspace's domain list, or the `allowedDomains` of a partner the owner administers) and the request
comes from another website (the `Origin` header, or the host of `Referer` when there is no `Origin`),
that composition is left out of `compositions` and reported in `errors` as
`Domain access denied: <reason>`; the others are still returned. A request that names no website, and
an owner who listed nothing, are not restricted, and a page on the visitor's own machine (`localhost`,
`127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`, on any port) is always allowed. So is the website where a partner integrates
Widgetic, with every subdomain of it (`platformDomain` in the answer of `GET /partners/mine`), for the
compositions of that partner: a partner's list never has to name it.

compositionIds.description: Array of composition IDs to retrieve

400.description: Invalid request

403.description: Domain access denied

Pass `managedUserId` (Widgetic's id for one of your managed users) or `managedUserExternalId` (your own
identifier for the user) to list only the canvases made for that managed user. The canvases of your other
managed users, and your own, are left out. A managed user that is not yours, or does not exist, is answered

post.summary: Add a document for a widget's AI to answer from
post.description:
Gives the widget's AI a document to answer visitors' questions from. Send the title and the plain text. The call
returns once the document is ready to be used, which takes a few seconds, longer for a long text.

**How it is used.** The text is cleaned, cut into short passages and each passage is turned into numbers (an
embedding) so the widget can find the passages nearest to a question. When a visitor asks, the nearest passages and
the question are shown to an AI model, which writes the answer from them and from nothing else; if the documents
say nothing about the question the visitor is told so, and the owner is not charged for that question. The titles of
the documents an answer used are shown to the visitor as its sources.

**What leaves Widgetic.** The text of a document is sent to OpenAI to be embedded when it is added, and the
passages used for a question are sent to the AI model that writes the answer. Say so in your privacy policy.

**Treat every document as public.** An answer can quote or paraphrase anything a document says, to any visitor of
the widget. Do not add passwords, keys, personal data or anything that must stay private.

**Limits.** A widget holds up to 20 documents, each up to 100000 characters, and up to 400000 characters in all
(`getAiAnswersKnowledge` reports the current numbers). Text only: convert PDF or Word files to text first. Adding a
document costs no credits. The same text cannot be added twice to one widget (409).

The caller must be allowed to change the widget. An API key needs the `content:write` scope. Adds are limited to ten
in ten minutes per person.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The widget (composition) to add the document to

201.description: The document was added and is ready to be used

400.description: The widget id is not valid, the body is not exactly `title` and `text`, or the title or the text is missing or too long (KNOWLEDGE_TITLE_REQUIRED, KNOWLEDGE_TITLE_TOO_LONG, KNOWLEDGE_TEXT_REQUIRED)

401.description: The API key is missing or invalid

403.description: The widget belongs to another account, or the API key lacks the `content:write` scope

404.description: There is no such widget

409.description: The same text is already in this widget, or the widget already holds the most documents it can (KNOWLEDGE_DUPLICATE_DOCUMENT, KNOWLEDGE_LIMIT_DOCUMENTS)

413.description: The text is longer than a document may be, or would take the widget past the most text it can hold in all (KNOWLEDGE_TEXT_TOO_LONG, KNOWLEDGE_LIMIT_TOTAL_TEXT). Nothing was saved

429.description: Too many documents added in a short time. Try again after the Retry-After seconds.

502.description: The document could not be processed or saved (KNOWLEDGE_NOT_COMPLETED). Nothing was saved: try again

503.description: The knowledge base is not available right now, or the service is busy (KNOWLEDGE_UNAVAILABLE, KNOWLEDGE_BUSY). Nothing was saved

Gives an adapter the key it needs to act through a service you have an account with, for the widgets you made.
Take the `adapterId` and `credentialKey` from `getUserAdapterConnections`. Saving a key that is already
connected replaces it.

credential, so that a stored value cannot be moved to another. It is never returned, never logged and never
shown to a visitor of a widget. A server of Widgetic opens it for the one call a widget makes through the

requestId.description: Names this attempt: 8 to 64 characters, letters, digits, `_` and `-`, the first a letter or a digit (a UUID fits). A module makes a new one for each action of the visitor. An operation that costs credits is charged once for each `requestId`, so a repeat of one that was charged and not given back is refused (409 `REQUEST_ALREADY_USED`) and does no work.

version.description: The version of the adapter the widget's code was built against (the `vN` of its import). When it is left out, the newest version the widget's live manifest lists.

input.description: What the operation is asked to do. Each operation says what it accepts and answers 400, 413 or 422 with a code of its own for what it cannot use. Defaults to an empty object.

context.description: The host context the embedding page gave the widget, as the entry route takes it (see the description of `createPublicCompositionEntry`, with its **Signed context**). It is not authenticated unless the partner signs it. At most 4096 bytes of JSON, the two signature keys included.

captchaToken.description: The visitor's CAPTCHA token, for an operation that asks for one (the answer `CAPTCHA_REQUIRED` says so).

output.description: What the operation answered, exactly as it wrote it: its field names are NOT rewritten to camelCase on the way out. At most 256 KiB of JSON. Each operation documents its own fields.

error.description: A sentence a visitor may read. It never says why a feature is unavailable: not that its owner is out of credits, not what a balance is, not which limit was reached beyond the word `RATE_LIMITED` or `WIDGET_LIMIT_REACHED`. (On a 429 the standard rate-limit envelope is sent instead: `error` is then an object, and `code` beside it is the flat code.)

code.description: What a module switches on. The codes of the gateway itself are `ADAPTER_BODY_INVALID`, `CAPTCHA_REQUIRED`, `ADAPTER_NOT_AVAILABLE`, `REQUEST_ALREADY_USED`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `WIDGET_LIMIT_REACHED`, `ADAPTER_FAILED`, `ADAPTER_UNAVAILABLE` and `ADAPTER_TIMEOUT`, with `ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, `PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE`, `UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE`, `CONTEXT_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED`, `CONTEXT_SIGNATURE_INVALID`, `CONTEXT_SIGNATURE_EXPIRED`, `CONTEXT_SIGNATURE_UNAVAILABLE` and the codes of the serving gate (`NOT_FOUND`, `UNPUBLISHED`, `SUSPENDED`) it shares with the other public embed routes. An operation may add codes of its own (capital letters and `_`) for an input it refused.

correlationId.description: Quote it when asking for help with a call.

PublicAdapterFileBytes.description: The bytes of the file as they are: no encoding and no form around them.

url.description: Where the stored file is. Always an https address.

name.description: The name it is stored under. It is not the name the visitor gave, which is only kept as far as it is plain text.

type.description: Its media type, as proved from its bytes.

width.description: The width in pixels of a picture, otherwise null.

height.description: The height in pixels of a picture, otherwise null.

PersonalWorkspaceDomain.description: One website on a person's own list of the websites allowed to show their widgets

id.description: The id of the entry. Use it to change or remove the entry

userId.description: The account the list belongs to

domain.description: The website as it is kept: lower case, with no scheme, port, path or leading `www.`. A leading `*.` means the website and all of its subdomains

ApiKeyScope.description:
One thing an API key may be allowed to do. A key made with a list of scopes does only what the list
names; a key made without one has full access, and does everything its owner can.

- `content:read` reads widgets, compositions, canvases, projects, folders, uploads, translations and the
  analytics of your content.
- `content:write` creates, changes, publishes and deletes the same. It includes `content:read`.
- `generate` runs the AI that builds widgets and compositions, and follows or cancels what it is doing.
  This spends credits.
- `partner:read` reads managed users, what they spent, presets, the contract and the storage destination.
- `partner:write` creates, changes and deletes managed users and presets. It includes `partner:read`.
- `billing:read` reads credits, usage, invoices, subscriptions and payment methods.
- `billing:write` buys credits, pays invoices and changes a subscription or a payment method. It
  includes `billing:read`.
- `account:read` reads the profile, organizations and members, allowed domains, notices and the names
  of API keys.
- `account:write` changes the profile, organizations and members, allowed domains and integrations. It
  includes `account:read`.

Starting an editor session for a managed user needs `partner:write`, `content:write` and `generate`
together. Making, changing and deleting keys, exchanging tokens, signing in and the administration
routes need full access: a limited key cannot make itself a bigger one.

A request outside the scopes of the key is refused with 403 and the code `API_KEY_SCOPE_MISSING`.
`error.details.missingScopes` names what a new key needs, and `error.details.fullAccessRequired` is true
when no list of scopes would have been enough. The scopes of a key cannot be changed once it is made.

UserApiKey.description: An API key of an account, as it is listed. It never carries the secret: that is shown once, in the answer to the request that made the key, and cannot be read again.

keyId.description: The id of the key. Use it to rename, switch off, delete or read the usage of the key

keyPreview.description: The first characters of the key, to tell keys apart. Not enough to use it

name.description: The name given to the key

expiresAt.description: When the key stops working. Absent or null when it does not expire

lastUsedAt.description: When the key was last used. Absent or null when it never was

isActive.description: Whether the key works. A key that is switched off is refused until it is switched on again

scopes.description: What the key may do. A key with full access holds every scope. The scopes of a key are fixed when it is made

preset.description: The name the scopes amount to. `full_access` is a key that is not limited, `read_only` and `content` are the ready-made lists, and `custom` is any other list

CreatedUserApiKey.description: A key that has just been made. It is the only answer that ever carries the secret, in `key`. Store it now: Widgetic keeps only a hash of it, and it cannot be shown again.

key.description: The secret. Send it as a bearer token, in the `Authorization` header. Shown once

scopes.description: What the key may do. A key made without scopes holds every scope

preset.description: The name the scopes amount to

name.description: A name for the key, to tell it from the account's other keys

expiresAt.description: When the key stops working, as a date and time in the future with a zone. Omit it for a key that does not expire

preset.description: A ready-made list of scopes. `read_only` looks at everything the account holds and changes nothing. `content` builds and manages widgets and compositions and runs the AI, and touches no billing, no people and no partners. `full_access` is the same as sending neither `preset` nor `scopes`. Send either `preset` or `scopes`, not both

scopes.description: What the key may do, when a preset is not enough. Naming a write scope includes its read scope, and a list that holds every scope is a key with full access. Send either `scopes` or `preset`, not both

UpdateUserApiKeyRequest.description: At least one of the two is required

name.description: A new name. It cannot be one that another key of the account already has

isActive.description: false switches the key off, true switches it on again. A key that is switched off stops working within a minute at the latest, and at once on the server that took the request

UserApiKeyUsageLog.description: One call made with a key

keyId.description: The key the call was made with

status.description: The HTTP status the call ended with

details.description: What was recorded about the call

Upload.description: A file stored for the account that uploaded it.

url.description: The public address of the stored file

mime_type.description: The type of the stored file. A HEIC or HEIF photo is stored as `image/jpeg`.

file_size.description: Size of the stored file, in bytes

storage_key.description: Where the file sits in its storage bucket

context_type.description: What the file was uploaded for. Media for widget content is `content-property`.

source.description: Which part of the product, or which client, uploaded the file. `widget-visitor-upload` is a file a visitor sent through a widget's upload adapter; it cannot be asked for when uploading.

managed_user_id.description: The managed user the file was uploaded for, or null when it is the account's own. List one managed user's files with the `managed_user_id` or `managed_user_external_id` query parameter of `uploadsGet`.

purpose.description: Where in the product the partner uses the file, or null when unknown

UploadLimits.description: What the upload endpoints accept. Read it rather than hard-coding the numbers.

multipart_max_bytes.description: The largest file `uploadsPost` takes in one request, in bytes. The same for every account.

multipart_mime_types.description: The file types `uploadsPost` takes for media (`content-property` uploads)

tus_enabled.description: Whether resumable uploads are switched on. They need a signed-in session; an API key uses `uploadsPost`.

tus_max_bytes.description: The largest file a resumable upload takes, in bytes (250 MB by default). The same for every account, whatever its plan. A file over `multipart_max_bytes` goes through a resumable upload.

tus_chunk_size_bytes.description: The chunk size resumable uploads are tuned for, in bytes. A client may send smaller or larger chunks.

MyPartner.description: A partner as the person who administers it reads it: which partner it is, what standing it is in, and why it is paused when it is. The webhook address, its secret and the billing settings have their own routes and are not part of it.

id.description: The id every other partner route asks for (`/partners/{partnerId}/...`)

status.description: `active` while the partner is in force. `inactive` until Widgetic activates it (and after a deactivation). `suspended` while it is paused, which is done by hand and comes back when Widgetic resumes it.

allowedDomains.description: The domains Widgetic added to the embeds of this partner's customers. The domains the person added themselves are on the domains route of the account.

platformDomain.description: The website where the partner integrates Widgetic, as a bare name. It and every subdomain of it (`app.acme.com`, `learn.eu.acme.com`) can always show the partner's widgets, the ones its customers make through it included, and send entries to them, whatever `allowedDomains` and the account's own domain list say, so a list can never lock the partner's own website out. It is not an entry of `allowedDomains`, and it does not turn an empty list into a restriction: a partner that lists nothing stays unrestricted for every website. Widgetic sets it when the partner is set up; contact Widgetic to change it. `null` when none has been set.

suspendedAt.description: When the partner was paused; null unless it is paused now

suspensionReason.description: The reason given when the partner was paused, as the partner is told it; null unless it is paused now

standing.description: The standing of the account as a whole, the word every gate reads: `not_a_partner` when the account administers no partner; otherwise `active` when any of its partners is in force, else `payment_arrears` when the partners that are active each have a contract invoice that is past its due date and unpaid, else `suspended` when any is paused, else `inactive`. `payment_arrears` is not set by anybody: it stops the same things a pause stops (billing, invoices, credits and the other routes a partner needs to pay stay open) and ends by itself the moment the invoice is paid.

overdueSince.description: When the oldest overdue contract invoice was due; null unless `standing` is `payment_arrears`. Pay the invoices in the list of `GET /invoices/partner/{partnerId}` that are past their due date to end it.

partners.description: The partners the account administers (nearly always one), the oldest first

usd.description: The dollars to spend on credits, to the cent: at least 10, at most 100000 in one request. The invoice is for the most whole credits that money buys at the list price of a credit, so it is never for more than this (12.34 buys 123 credits and the invoice says 12.30).

PartnerExtraCreditsInvoice.description: The invoice for extra credits that was issued, and what paying it adds.

number.description: The number printed on the invoice, once Stripe has numbered it.

hostedInvoiceUrl.description: The page where the invoice is viewed and paid.

credits.description: The credits paying the invoice adds, once and for good. They do not expire.

creditPriceUsd.description: What one credit costs, in dollars. It is the list price, not the price of the contract.

amountUsd.description: The price of those credits, in dollars, before tax. Never more than `usd` of the request.

taxUsd.description: The tax added to the invoice, in dollars (0 when there is none).

totalUsd.description: What is paid, in dollars. The price plus the tax.

currency.description: The currency of the invoice, in upper case (USD).

dueDate.description: When payment is due, as printed on the invoice.

dueDays.description: How many days there are to pay.

PartnerContract.description: The commercial terms agreed with a partner. Prices are in dollars. Internal negotiation notes and the staff members who edited the record are not part of it.

customPrice.description: The agreed price per `billingCycle`; null when the standard price applies

customCredits.description: Credits received each billing period (`billingCycle`); null when the standard allowance applies

creditPriceUsd.description: The agreed price of one credit, in dollars; null when the list price applies

effectiveCreditPriceUsd.description: What one credit costs you, in dollars. The agreed price, or the list price when none was agreed

periodTotalUsd.description: What one billing period costs, in dollars before tax, `customCredits` times `effectiveCreditPriceUsd`. Null while no credits were agreed

additionalFeatures.description: Features included beyond the standard partner plan

contractEndDate.description: Null when the contract runs until it is ended

isActiveContract.description: True while the contract is in force, that is when it is open-ended or today falls between its start and end

PartnerStorageDestination.description: The bucket a partner keeps the files its account uploads in: a bucket on an S3-compatible service that the partner owns. The secret access key is never returned.

endpoint.description: The HTTPS address of the S3-compatible service, scheme and host only

keyPrefix.description: The folder inside the bucket every file is written under. Empty, or folders each followed by a slash.

publicBaseUrl.description: Where the stored files are served from. A file's url is this address, a slash and the file's key.

forcePathStyle.description: Whether the bucket name goes in the path of a request (true) or in the host name (false)

accessKeyHint.description: The last four characters of the access key id, to tell which key is set. Not enough to use it.

verifiedAt.description: When the destination last passed the check

lastVerificationError.description: Why the most recent re-check failed. Null while the last check passed.

SetPartnerStorageDestinationRequest.description: The bucket to keep the partner's files in, and the key that may write to it. These field names are snake_case, as in every request.

endpoint.description: The HTTPS address of the S3-compatible service, scheme and host only (no path, port or credentials). It must be a host name, not an IP address, and must resolve to the public internet.

region.description: The region the service signs requests for. Use auto where the service says so.

key_prefix.description: A folder inside the bucket to write every file under, for example widgetic/uploads. Folders are made of letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores. Leave it out to write at the root of the bucket.

public_base_url.description: Where the stored files are served from: the bucket's public address, or a CDN in front of it. The address of a file is this value, a slash and the file's key in the bucket, which starts with the key prefix. A path is allowed (https://f000.backblazeb2.com/file/acme-widget-media).

force_path_style.description: Put the bucket name in the path of a request. Every S3-compatible service supports this; set it to false only for a service that needs the bucket name in the host name.

access_key_id.description: The id of an access key that may put objects into the bucket

secret_access_key.description: The secret of that access key. It is stored encrypted and is never returned.

removed.description: False when the partner had no storage destination to remove

PartnerPreset.description: A widget the partner offers its managed users as a starting point, under a key the partner's code names. It belongs to the partner's account, so every managed user of the partner sees the same list.

key.description: The name the partner's code uses for the preset

widgetId.description: The partner's widget. Use it to make a composition (`createComposition` with this `widgetId`).

title.description: What the partner's picker shows. Null means show `widgetName`.

position.description: The list is ordered by this, smallest first, then by key

thumbnailUrl.description: The widget's thumbnail, when it has one

widgetId.description: One of the partner's own widgets. A widget is a preset under at most one key.

title.description: What your picker shows. Leave it out to show the widget's own name.

position.description: Where the preset sits in the list. Smallest first; presets with the same position are ordered by key.

removed.description: False when there was no preset under that key

PartnerReportPage.description: Which part of a list the answer holds.

limit.description: How many rows the page can hold at most

offset.description: How many rows were skipped before this page

hasMore.description: True when more rows follow this page. Ask again with `offset` raised by `limit`.

PartnerReportPeriod.description: The stretch of time a report covers.

to.description: End of the period, not included

PartnerStorageUsageTotals.description: What a group of files weigh, and how much of it is kept where.

totalBytes.description: The size of all the files together, in bytes

widgeticStorageBytes.description: The part of `totalBytes` that is kept in Widgetic's storage

partnerStorageBytes.description: The part of `totalBytes` that is kept in your own storage destination

PartnerStorageUsageOfManagedUser.description: The files filed under one managed user. The row with a null `managedUserId` is the files that are not filed under any: your own, and the ones uploaded without naming a managed user.

managedUserId.description: Widgetic's id for the managed user. Null for the files that are not filed under one.

externalId.description: Your own identifier for the managed user

isActive.description: False when the managed user is switched off

lastUploadAt.description: When the newest of these files was stored

PartnerStorageUsage.description: What a partner's customers store. `totals` is every file kept for the partner's account; `managedUsers` splits it by the managed user each file is filed under, the heaviest first.

PartnerAnalyticsSummary.description: What was done with the partner's published widgets in a period.

managedUserId.description: The managed user the report is narrowed to. Null for the whole account.

views.description: How many times a composition was shown to a visitor

interactions.description: How many times a visitor did something with a composition

visitors.description: How many different visitors viewed. A visitor is a browsing session; an event that carries no session is counted for the signed-in user instead. An event that carries neither is a view and no visitor.

compositionsViewed.description: How many different compositions were viewed

managedUsersViewed.description: How many different managed users had a composition viewed

PartnerAnalyticsOfManagedUser.description: What one managed user's widgets and compositions did in a period.

externalId.description: Your own identifier for the managed user

widgetsMade.description: How many widgets are filed under the managed user (all time, not only in the period)

compositionsMade.description: How many compositions are filed under the managed user (all time, not only in the period)

lastEventAt.description: When the newest counted view or interaction happened. Null when there was none in the period.

PartnerAnalyticsByManagedUser.description: What each of the partner's managed users did in a period. Every managed user of the partner is listed, also one whose widgets were not viewed, the most viewed first.

PartnerAnalyticsOfWidget.description: What one widget's compositions did in a period.

widgetName.description: Null when the widget has been deleted since

compositionsViewed.description: How many different compositions of the widget were viewed

PartnerAnalyticsTopWidgets.description: The widgets whose compositions were viewed the most in a period, the most viewed first.

managedUserId.description: The managed user the report is narrowed to. Null for the whole account.

PartnerAnalyticsOfDay.description: What was done on one day (UTC).

PartnerAnalyticsTimeline.description: What was done on each day of a period.

managedUserId.description: The managed user the report is narrowed to. Null for the whole account.

days.description: One entry for every day of the period, oldest first. A day nothing happened on is all zeros.

PartnerNotificationEventType.description: What happened. The event types you can be told about.

PartnerNotification.description: One thing that happened to your partner account. The same object is what your webhook receives as `data` of a call (beside `id`, `type`, `createdAt` and `partnerId`), and what the list in your dashboard shows.

title.description: One line that says what happened

body.description: A few sentences that say what happened and what to do about it

data.description: The facts of the event, named in camelCase. An invoice event carries `invoiceNumber`, `subtotal`, `taxAmount`, `total`, `currency`, `dueDate`, `hostedInvoiceUrl` (the page where it is paid) and `purpose` (`contract`, or `extra_credits` for credits you bought on top of the contract: an unpaid invoice for extra credits never stops the account, the credits are just not added until it is paid); a payment adds `paidAt`, a failed payment `reason`, a reminder `daysUntilDue` or `daysOverdue`. A credits event carries `band` (`low` or `empty`), `balance` and `threshold`. `credits.managed_user_cap_reached` (one of your managed users used its monthly credits and a request was refused) goes to your webhook only when subscribed, once per managed user each month, and carries `managedUserId`, `externalId`, `monthlyCredits`, `creditsUsed`, `resetsAt` and `reachedAt`. A standing event carries `status`, `previousStatus` and `reason`; `partner.paused` with `status: payment_arrears` means that an overdue invoice stopped the account (nobody paused it, and `reason` names the invoice), and `partner.resumed` with `previousStatus: payment_arrears` means that its payment ended that. A storage event carries `reason` and `checkedAt`. Content events (`composition.created`, `composition.updated`, `widget.published`, `upload.created`, `entry.created`) go to your webhook only when subscribed; they do not appear in the dashboard list. `composition.created` carries `compositionId`, `widgetId`, `name`, `managedUserId`, `externalId` and `createdAt`; `composition.updated` carries `compositionId`, `widgetId`, `name`, `managedUserId`, `externalId`, `contentVersion` and `savedAt`, and is sent for the first save of a composition in each five minutes (read the composition for its current state); `widget.published` carries `widgetId`, `name`, `managedUserId`, `externalId`, `version` and `publishedAt`; `upload.created` carries `uploadId`, `name`, `mimeType`, `sizeBytes`, `address`, `managedUserId`, `externalId`, `purpose` and `createdAt`; `entry.created` carries `compositionId`, `table`, `entryId`, `createdAt` and `context` (the host attribution of the embedding page, or null), and none of the values the visitor entered: read those with the entries routes. Ignore an event type you do not know: more may be added. `sendPartnerNotificationTestEvent` sends a sample of every one of them.

PartnerNotificationPage.description: A page of notifications, the newest first.

nextBefore.description: Send as `before` to get the next, older page. Null when there is none.

PartnerNotificationDelivery.description: One send of one notification, to one email address or to your webhook. It stays `pending` while it is being tried again, and ends `delivered`, `failed` (given up on) or `cancelled` (nobody wanted it any more, for example because the webhook was switched off).

eventType.description: What the notification was about. Null when the notification has been removed.

target.description: The email address, or the host of your webhook (never the whole address, which may hold a token)

nextAttemptAt.description: When the next attempt is made. Null once the delivery has ended.

lastStatusCode.description: The HTTP status your webhook answered with at the last attempt, when it answered

lastError.description: Why the last attempt failed, in a few words. Never what your endpoint replied.

replayOfDeliveryId.description: When this row is a manual replay, the earlier delivery it sent again

PartnerNotificationDeliveryLog.description: How the notifications reached their addresses, the newest first.

PartnerNotificationEvent.description: One kind of event you can be told about.

description.description: One sentence that says when it happens

alwaysEmailed.description: True for money and standing: you are emailed whatever you chose, and can narrow only what your own system receives.

delivery.description: `all`: email (when chosen), dashboard inbox and webhook. `webhook`: signed call only — no email and not listed in the dashboard inbox.

PartnerNotificationDefaultRecipients.description: Who gets the emails while you have given no addresses of your own.

payments.description: For the invoice events, the billing emails of your billing profile, or your contact email when there are none

other.description: For every other event, your contact email

PartnerNotificationSettings.description: Where your notifications go. The secret that signs your webhook is never part of it.

emailRecipients.description: The addresses the emails go to. Empty means the defaults.

emailEvents.description: The events you want by email. Null means every event. The events marked `alwaysEmailed` are emailed whatever it says.

webhookUrl.description: Where Widgetic sends a signed call for each event. Null while the webhook is switched off.

webhookEvents.description: The events sent to your webhook. Null means every event.

webhookSecretSet.description: Whether a signing secret exists. Calls are made only when it does.

webhookSecretRotatedAt.description: When the current secret was made

webhookSigningAvailable.description: False when this server cannot sign webhooks, in which case a webhook cannot be set up yet

events.description: Every event there is, for a settings screen to list

UpdatePartnerNotificationSettingsRequest.description: What to change. A key you leave out is left as it was.

emailRecipients.description: The addresses the emails go to, at most five. An empty list goes back to the defaults.

emailEvents.description: The events you want by email. Null for every event.

webhookEvents.description: The events to send to your webhook. Null for every event.

webhookUrl.description: Where to send the signed calls. It must be an https address on the standard port, on a public site, and it must not redirect. Null or an empty text switches the webhook off. Setting an address when you have no secret yet makes one.

PartnerNotificationSettingsChange.description: The settings after a change, and the new signing secret when one was made.

webhookSecret.description: The secret that signs your webhook, in the form your receiver is configured with (`whsec_...`). It is in this answer ONLY: keep it now, it cannot be read again. Null when the change made no secret.

PartnerNotificationTestEventRequest.description: Which kind of event to send a sample of.

PartnerNotificationTestEventResult.description: How a test call went. The call was made whether or not your receiver took it: read `delivered`.

delivered.description: True when your receiver answered with a 2xx status.

statusCode.description: The HTTP status your receiver answered with. Null when it did not answer (refused, unreachable or too slow).

durationMs.description: How long the call took, in milliseconds. A call is given up after ten seconds.

error.description: Why the call did not arrive, in a few words (`timeout`, `status 500`, `unreachable`, a redirect). Never what your receiver replied. Left out when it arrived.

PartnerEntryContextSigning.description: How the context of your embeds is signed. The secret that signs it is never part of this: it is shown once, when it is made.

required.description: True: an entry whose context carries no valid signature is refused (403 `CONTEXT_SIGNATURE_REQUIRED`). False: an entry that carries a signature is checked, and one that carries none is accepted as before.

secretSet.description: Whether you have a signing secret. Until you have, no signature is checked and none can be required.

secretRotatedAt.description: When the current secret was made. Null while there is none.

previousSecretValidUntil.description: While you switch to a new secret, when the secret it replaced stops being accepted. Null when there is none to wait for.

signingAvailable.description: False when this server cannot keep secrets, in which case none can be made yet.

required.description: True to refuse every entry whose context carries no valid signature. False to check the signature of the entries that carry one and accept the others, as before.

PartnerEntryContextSecret.description: A new signing secret, and how your signing stands now.

secret.description: The secret: `ctxsec_` followed by the base64 of 32 random bytes. It is shown here, once, and cannot be read again.

PartnerDataDatabase.description: The Neon database your compositions keep what visitors leave in them (votes, ratings, answers, form submissions). The connection string and its password are never part of this: they are given once, when the database is set.

host.description: The Neon host of the database, as it appears in its connection string (`ep-....neon.tech`).

databaseName.description: The name of the database in your Neon project.

verifiedAt.description: When the database last passed the check.

lastVerificationError.description: Why the latest re-check failed, in a sentence you can act on. Null when the last check passed.

lastVerificationFailedAt.description: When the latest re-check failed. Null when the last check passed.

connectionString.description: The connection string of a Neon database and role you made for this, as Neon shows it under Connect: `postgresql://<role>:<password>@ep-<name>.<region>.aws.neon.tech/<database>`. Either the direct or the pooled host works. Everything after the database name (`?sslmode=...`) is ignored. It is stored encrypted and is never returned or logged.

removed.description: False when the partner had no database of its own to remove

domain.description: Domain pattern to allow (supports wildcards like *.example.com)

url.description: URL of the pre-uploaded content item.

file_size.description: Size of the file in bytes.

metadata.description: Additional metadata for the content item (e.g., image dimensions, duration).

display_order.description: The display order of this attachment within the message. Lower numbers appear first.

message_content.description: Primary text content of the message. Required if attachments are not provided.
message_content.example: Hello, can you update the hero section?

attachments.description: Optional array of file attachments. Required if message_content is not provided.

suggestions.description: Follow-up chips of a clarification card riding an assistant message. At most six; each has a display `label` and the `intent` its chip carries. Omit the property for a message without a card.

label.description: Display copy for the chip. Never parsed by the client.

intent.description: The machine-readable behavior the chip carries.

design_controls.description: The inline design-control card this reply carries, when the host applied a directed design tweak with no codegen. Persisted with the reply so a chat reload re-renders the card instead of showing the text alone. The payload is `{ summary, properties: [{ id, label, controllerType, value, ... }], compositionId }`; `compositionId` records the composition the change was authored against, which is what lets the host re-attach the card to that composition's live design values after a reload.

user_id.description: ID of the user sending the message

example.message_content: Hello, can you update the hero section?

UpdateMessageRequest.description: At least one property must be provided for an update. A message's design-control card is not updatable here: an edit has nothing to say about it, and the update RPC leaves the column untouched, so it survives edits to the text.

message_content.description: Updated primary text content of the message.

attachments.description: Updated array of file attachments. If provided, replaces all existing attachments.

suggestions.description: Replacement clarification-card suggestions on this message. If provided, replaces the stored suggestions (an empty array clears them); omit the property to leave them untouched, so an edit that only rewrites the text cannot drop a card's chips.

label.description: Display copy for the chip. Never parsed by the client.

intent.description: The machine-readable behavior the chip carries.

ManagedUser.description: A managed user as the API answers. The answer names its fields in camelCase (`externalId`), while the request that creates or changes a managed user names them in snake_case (`external_id`).

id.description: Unique identifier for the managed user

managerId.description: ID of the user who manages this managed user

externalId.description: Your own identifier for the managed user. Unique among the managed users you manage (two different partners may use the same value).

metadata.description: Additional metadata for the managed user

isActive.description: Whether new compositions, widgets and uploads can be filed under this managed user. `false` means it has been switched off (`updateManagedUser` with `is_active: false`): what it already has stays, and filing anything new under it answers `409 MANAGED_USER_INACTIVE`. A record from before the switch existed may answer `null`, which counts as on.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the managed user was created

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the managed user was last updated

external_id.description: Your own identifier for the managed user. Must be unique among the managed users you manage (409 otherwise); another partner using the same value does not matter.

manager_id.description: ID of the user who will manage this managed user. Defaults to your own user ID; a partner can only use their own ID (403 otherwise), only an admin can name another manager.

metadata.description: Additional metadata for the managed user

external_id.description: Updated external identifier for the managed user. Must be unique among the managed users you manage (409 otherwise).

metadata.description: Updated additional metadata for the managed user

is_active.description: Switch the managed user off (`false`) or back on (`true`). A managed user that is off keeps everything already filed under it, and that content can still be listed, but nothing new can be filed under it (`409 MANAGED_USER_INACTIVE`). Send a real boolean, not the text "false". Switching a managed user off also ends all of its editor sessions.

surfaces.description: The pieces of Widgetic's editor the session may drive. `files` is the media library (the File Browser: upload a file, list the files uploaded for this user); what a user uploads is kept in your own storage destination. Partner storage is not optional: a session of any surface can be made only once you have set a destination up (`setPartnerStorageDestination`), and is refused with `409 PARTNER_STORAGE_REQUIRED` until then. `editor` is editing one of this user's compositions: read it, change its name, content, design and embed settings, read its schemas, and ask where to show it (`getCompositionPreview`: the widget's published page). `creator` is Widgetic's widget creator, with its drawing canvas and its AI: this user's canvases, the widgets on them and the conversation of each widget, the generation, build and publish calls that make a widget, and the compositions of those widgets (list, make). The surfaces do not imply one another: the whole creator also saves a composition (`editor`) and attaches pictures to its chat (`files`), so ask for `["creator", "editor", "files"]`.

expires_in_seconds.description: How long the session lasts, in seconds. It cannot be extended; make a new session when it ends.

allowed_origin.description: Bind the session to one web page origin, such as `https://app.example.com` (no path; `http` is accepted only for `localhost`). The session is then refused from any other origin, and from a request that carries no `Origin` header. Leave it out for a session that can be used from anywhere, which is what a server-side caller needs.

max_credits.description: The most credits this session may spend on Widgetic's AI, one credit being one generation. Once the operations it ran have taken that many, the next one is refused (402, `EDITOR_SESSION_CREDIT_LIMIT_REACHED`) and the browser is only told that the feature is not available right now. A generation that fails is refunded and does not count. Leave it out to get the limit Widgetic has set for your account, if it has set one (it sets none unless you ask), and otherwise no limit of its own, which leaves the credits of your account as the only ceiling. Send `null` to ask for no limit of its own even when a default is set.

EditorSession.description: An editor session you have just made. `token` is shown once and cannot be read again: hand it to the browser of this one user and keep it out of logs and storage.

token.description: The credential the browser sends as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It starts with `wgt_ses_`. It works only for the calls of the session's surfaces, only for this managed user's content, and only until `expiresAt`.

sessionId.description: Identifies the session, so you can end it (`revokeManagedUserEditorSession`). It is not a credential.

managedUserExternalId.description: Your own identifier for the managed user

allowedOrigin.description: The web page origin the session is bound to, or null when it is not bound

maxCredits.description: The most credits the session may spend on Widgetic's AI (`max_credits`), or null when it has no limit of its own

ManagedUserOperationUsage.description: What one metered operation cost a managed user's editor sessions over the period

operation.description: The metered operation, as the credit ledger names it

calls.description: How many runs of the operation were paid for and kept (a run that was refunded is not one)

credits.description: The credits those runs took from your account

refundedCalls.description: How many runs were refunded (a generation that failed), and so are not in `calls`

refundedCredits.description: The credits the refunded runs took, which went back to your account

ManagedUserUsage.description: What a managed user's editor sessions spent over a period. Only credits taken through editor sessions are counted, from the day usage was first recorded: what you spend with your API key is not, and neither is anything from before.

managedUserExternalId.description: Your own identifier for the managed user

to.description: End of the period, not included

operations.description: One entry for each operation that was paid for in the period, in alphabetical order

name.description: Names the copy. Left out, the copy is named after the preset's title, or the widget's own name.

PartnerPresetCopy.description: Where the copy of a preset is. Open the widget creator on `canvasId` and `widgetId`.

managedUserId.description: The managed user the copy was made for

canvasId.description: The new canvas the copy is on

widgetId.description: The new widget, which is not a preset and which only this managed user's editor reaches

warnings.description: Things that did not go as planned but did not stop the copy. Empty when everything did.

PartnerInvoice.description: An invoice issued to a partner. Money is in dollars (not cents). Administrator notes, billing-provider identifiers and Widgetic account ids are not part of what a partner is sent.

number.description: The number printed on the invoice, once it has been issued

amount.description: Total, in dollars. The price plus the tax (the same number as `total`)

subtotal.description: The price, before tax, in dollars

taxAmount.description: The tax on the price, in dollars. 0 when there is none, for example under the EU reverse charge

total.description: What the partner pays, in dollars. The price plus the tax

amountDue.description: What is still owed, in dollars

amountPaid.description: What has been paid, in dollars

failureReason.description: Why the last attempt to pay failed, in the payment provider's words for the card holder. Null unless the status is `failed`; the invoice stays payable from `hostedInvoiceUrl`

status.description: `open` waits for payment, `failed` waits for payment after an attempt was refused, `paid` is settled (a payment received outside the payment provider counts), `void` was cancelled and owes nothing, and `uncollectible` was written off

paymentMethod.description: How it was paid, once it was

hostedInvoiceUrl.description: The page where the invoice can be viewed and paid, once it has been issued

pdfUrl.description: A PDF of the invoice, once it has been issued

Entitlement.description: Feature entitlement for users, partners, or managed users

userId.description: ID of the user (if user-level entitlement)

partnerId.description: ID of the partner (if partner-level entitlement)

managedUserId.description: ID of the managed user (if managed user-level entitlement)

feature.description: Feature identifier that this entitlement grants access to

value.description: Value or limit for this feature

expiresAt.description: When this entitlement expires (null for permanent)

sourceId.description: ID of the source object that granted this entitlement

updatedAt.description: When the entitlement was last updated

EntitlementCheck.description: Result of checking a specific entitlement

userId.description: ID of the user who was checked

entitled.description: Whether the user has this entitlement

AccountCreditBalance.description: The credits an account holds. Credits are held per user, so the same balance applies in a personal workspace and in an organization the user belongs to.

reservedBalance.description: Credits committed to an operation that is still running. They cannot be spent, so what a new operation can use is `balance - reservedBalance`.

AccountCreditTransaction.description: One entry of an account's credit ledger.

transactionType.description: What the entry did to the balance. `debit` is credits spent (this is how consumption shows), `credit` and `subscription` are credits added, `refund` returns credits that were spent, `reserve` and `release` move credits in and out of the reserved amount, and `adjustment`, `expiration`, `transfer_out` and `transfer_in` are the remaining ways a balance changes. The list can grow, so treat an unknown type as an entry you do not need to interpret.

amount.description: Always positive. The `transactionType` says whether the credits were added or taken.

balanceAfter.description: The balance once this entry was applied

referenceId.description: The event the entry belongs to. An entry is recorded once per reference.

creatorId.description: ID of the user who created the composition

widgetId.description: ID of the widget this composition is based on

contentVersion.description: Monotonic content version when the content_version migration is applied

updatedAt.description: When the composition was last updated

databaseId.description: Legacy. The id of a Neon database that an earlier version made for this composition. A composition now keeps its tables in a schema of its own (named `comp_` followed by its id) in a database shared with other compositions, so new compositions have none.

projectId.description: ID of the project this composition belongs to

managedUserId.description: The managed user the composition was made for, or null when it is your own. List one managed user's compositions with the `managedUserId` or `managedUserExternalId` query parameter of `getAllCompositions`.

direct.description:
Whether the widget the composition is made from is drawn straight into the page, without a frame
(`true`), or inside a frame (`false`). `null` when the widget has no published version yet. It is a
fact about the widget's published version, so every composition of one widget answers the same, and it
changes when you publish another version. It cannot be set. Only `getCompositionById` returns it:
the other calls that return a composition leave it out, and so does that one on the rare occasion the
answer could not be worked out just then (ask again).

widgetId.description: ID of the widget this composition is based on

creatorId.description: ID of the user creating the composition

databaseSchema.description:
The tables this composition keeps what visitors send it in (votes, ratings, answers). They are made when
the composition is created, in a schema of their own that no other composition can reach: in Widgetic's
database, or in your own Neon database when you have set one with `setPartnerDataDatabase`. They are
deleted with the composition.

The shape is `{ "tables": [ ... ] }`. A table has a `name`, a list of `columns` and, optionally, a list of
`indexes`. A column has a `name` and a `type`, and optionally `primaryKey`, `notNull`, `unique` and
`default`. An index has a `name` and the `columns` it covers (1 to 8), and optionally `unique`. Any other
key is refused.

- Names (tables, columns, indexes) use lower-case letters, digits and underscores, start with a letter and
  are at most 63 characters long. A name that starts with `_` or `pg_` is reserved.
- `type` is one of `text`, `smallint`, `integer` (or `int`), `bigint`, `numeric`, `real`,
  `double precision`, `boolean` (or `bool`), `date`, `timestamp`, `timestamptz` (or
  `timestamp with time zone`), `uuid`, `json`, `jsonb`, `serial`, `bigserial`.
- `default` is a number, `true` or `false`, a text of at most 500 characters (no backslash), a JSON value
  for a `json` or `jsonb` column, or one of `now()`, `current_timestamp` and `current_date` (date and
  timestamp columns) and `gen_random_uuid()` (a `uuid` column). A `serial` column numbers itself and has
  no default.
- A composition declares at most 20 tables, with at most 64 columns and 10 indexes each.

A declaration that cannot be used is refused with `400` and `INVALID_DATABASE_SCHEMA`;
`error.details.problems` lists what to change. Tables that already exist are never changed or dropped:
sending more tables later, when you update the composition, adds the ones that are missing. When the
composition is saved but its tables cannot be made just now, the answer says so in `meta.warnings`: send
the same `databaseSchema` again to retry.

projectId.description: ID of the project this composition belongs to

managedUserId.description: Make the composition for one of your managed users, by Widgetic's id for the user. Send this or `managedUserExternalId`, not both. The managed user must be yours and active. The composition stays in your account; the tag lets you list one user's compositions and keeps it out of the others' lists. It is set here and does not change afterwards.

managedUserExternalId.description: The same, by your own identifier for the user, the `external_id` you gave when you created the managed user (answers show it as `externalId`). Send this or `managedUserId`, not both.

databaseSchema.description:
Tables to make for the composition, in the shape `createComposition` takes
(`{ "tables": [ ... ] }`, with the same names, types, defaults and limits). Only the tables that are
missing are made. A table that already exists is never changed or dropped: it keeps its columns, so a
column added to the declaration is not added to it. A declaration that cannot be used is refused with
`400` and `INVALID_DATABASE_SCHEMA`. When the composition is saved but its tables cannot be made just
now, `meta.warnings` says so: send the same `databaseSchema` again to retry.

name.description: The column's name exactly as the database spells it. Pass it as `groupBy` to tally by it.
The table's name exactly as the database spells it. Pass it as `table` to read it.

columns.description: The table's columns, in table order (up to 40)

rows.description: How many entries the table holds. `null` when they could not be counted, which is not zero.

compositionId.description: The composition whose entries these are

hasData.description:
False when the composition keeps no entries of its own: its widget only shows content (it has no
database), or nothing was set up in the database yet. That is not an error.

tables.description: The tables entries are kept in (up to 20)

value.description:
One value of the column, as text (a number is `"5"`, a yes/no is `"true"`), cut to 200 characters.
`null` groups the entries that left the column empty.

count.description: How many entries have that value

compositionId.description: The composition whose entries these are

totalRows.description:
How many entries the table holds in all. Not narrowed by `since`, `until` or a filter: only
`aggregates` is.

tallies.description:
How many entries have each value of the `groupBy` column, largest group first (up to 20 groups), over
the whole table. `null` when no `groupBy` was asked for. For the groups of a selection (a time window,
a `context` filter) or for more than 20 groups, ask for `aggregate`: `aggregates.tallies` holds up to
200 groups.

moreGroups.description:
True when the `groupBy` column has more than the 20 groups `tallies` lists. It speaks of `tallies`
only: `aggregates.truncated` is the same signal for `aggregates` (200 groups).

columns.description:
The name of each value of an entry in `rows`, in order, exactly as the database spells it (and as
`describeCompositionEntries` lists it: `created_at` stays `created_at`). Empty when no entries were
asked for, or the table has none.

rows.description:
The newest entries, newest first (up to 25). `null` when no entries were asked for. Each entry is a
list of values in the order of `columns`. A value is text (cut to 200 characters), a number, a
boolean or `null`.

items.description: A text, a number, a boolean or null

moreRows.description: True when the table holds more entries than `rows` lists

aggregates.description:
Only present when the read asked for `aggregate`. Unlike `totalRows`, `tallies` and `rows`, it is
narrowed by `since`, `until` and the `context` and column filters of the same call: it answers
"the average rating this week" where `tallies` answer "how many of each rating, ever".

CompositionDataSource.description:
The public JSON address a composition's widget reads when it loads and again every `refreshSeconds`. One
per composition: binding another replaces it. It is sent as `refresh_seconds` (the request body keeps the
snake case it always had) and answered as `refreshSeconds`, like every answer of the API.

url.description: The https address as it was saved, after the checks (a public host, never loopback, link-local or a metadata address)

refreshSeconds.description: How often the widget reads the address again, in seconds

persistenceKey.description: Key used for persistent storage and reference

canvasContent.description: JSON content of the canvas, containing layout and configuration

creatorId.description: UUID of the user who created the canvas

primaryWidgetId.description: Primary widget for My widgets list and canvas-only deep-link (Convert per shape may add secondary widgets on the same canvas)

managedUserId.description: The managed user the canvas was made for (Widgetic's id for the user); null for a canvas that is the account's own.

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the canvas was created

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the canvas was last updated

persistenceKey.description: Key used for persistent storage and reference

canvasContent.description: JSON content of the canvas, containing layout and configuration

primaryWidgetId.description: Optional primary widget id (usually set after widget create)

managedUserId.description: Make the canvas for this managed user (Widgetic's id for the user). Send this or `managedUserExternalId`, not both. The tag is set here and does not change afterwards.

managedUserExternalId.description: Make the canvas for the managed user you registered with this `external_id` (your own identifier for the user). Send this or `managedUserId`, not both.

projectId.description: Project this canvas belongs to. Empty canvases show on that project's list.

persistenceKey.description: Updated key used for persistent storage and reference

canvasContent.description: Updated JSON content of the canvas

primaryWidgetId.description: Primary widget for list/deep-link; omit to leave unchanged

statusCode.description: HTTP status code of the operation

id.description: Unique identifier for the event record

composition_id.description: ID of the composition this event is for

event_type.description: Type of event (view, interaction, click, etc.)

event_data.description: Additional event data as JSON object

user_id.description: ID of the user who triggered the event

session_id.description: ID of the session when the event occurred

user_agent.description: User agent string of the browser
