event_type.description: Type of event (view, interaction, click, etc.)

event_data.description: Additional event data as JSON object

user_id.description: ID of the user who triggered the event

session_id.description: ID of the session when the event occurred

user_agent.description: User agent string of the browser

AiAnswersKnowledgeDocument.description: One document in a widget's knowledge base: what the widget's AI answers visitors' questions from. Its text is not part of this: it is kept so the widget can find the passages that answer a question, and is never returned.

id.description: Use it to remove the document

title.description: What the document is called. Visitors see it as the source of an answer, so write it for them

status.description: `ready` documents are used to answer questions. A `processing` document is not: it is being added, or an add was interrupted. Remove one that stays in this state and add it again

charCount.description: How many characters of text the document holds, after it was cleaned

chunkCount.description: Into how many passages the text was cut. Zero until the document is ready

readyAt.description: When the document became ready. Null while it is not

documents.description: How many documents the widget has

characters.description: How many characters of text they hold in all

maxDocuments.description: The most documents one widget can hold

maxTotalChars.description: The most characters of text one widget's documents can hold in all

title.description: What the document is called, on one line. Visitors see it as the source of an answer. Line breaks and invisible characters are removed

text.description: The text of the document, as plain text. It is cleaned (line endings are made the same, invisible characters and surplus blank lines are removed) and then counted: up to 100000 characters. Markup is not interpreted, so paste the words, not a web page
text.example: Orders ship within 2 business days. Returns are accepted for 30 days after delivery, in the original packaging.

example.title: Shipping and returns
example.text: Orders ship within 2 business days. Returns are accepted for 30 days after delivery, in the original packaging.

removed.description: Always true. A document that was not there is a 404 instead

AdapterConnection.description: A key an adapter can take from an account, and whether the account has connected it. The key itself is never part of this: it is given once, when it is connected, and Widgetic keeps it encrypted.

adapterId.description: The adapter the key is for (its id in the adapter catalog)

adapterLabel.description: What the adapter is called to its owner

credentialKey.description: The name of the key within the adapter. Use it, with the adapter id, to connect or remove the key

label.description: What the key is called to its owner

scope.description: Who may keep this key. `owner` is the person who made the widget, in their own account. `partner` is a partner, for the widgets of the customers it manages. `owner_or_partner` is either; for a widget of a managed customer the partner's key is used.

connected.description: Whether this account has connected the key

updatedAt.description: When the key was last set. Null when it is not connected

credential.description: The key exactly as its provider gave it: one line of text, at most 2048 characters. It is stored encrypted and is never returned or logged.

removed.description: False when the key was not connected, so there was nothing to remove

UpdateDomainRequest.description: The body of a request that changes an entry of a list of allowed websites. The property is `domain`, as when an entry is added: the routes read nothing called `name`.

domain.description: The website name to keep instead, such as `example.com`, or `*.example.com` for a website and all of its subdomains

Widget.description: Represents a widget in the system.

creatorId.description: ID of the user who created the widget.

description.description: Description of the widget's purpose and functionality.
description.example: Interactive chart widget for data visualization

type.description: Type of widget (e.g., chart, form, gallery).

isPublic.description: Whether the widget is publicly available.

isDraft.description: Whether the widget is a draft.

shareId.description: Unique ID for sharing the widget publicly.

updatedAt.description: When the widget was last updated.

jsPath.description: Path to the JavaScript file for this widget.

canvasId.description: ID of the canvas associated with this widget.

databaseId.description: Legacy. The name of a Neon database that an earlier version made for this widget. A widget has no database now (what the visitors of a composition leave is kept in the tables of that composition), so widgets made now have none.

cpgSchemaId.description: ID linking to the widget's code graph schema.

lastCpgCommitSha.description: Last Git commit SHA analyzed for code graph.

organizationId.description: Organization ID if created in an organization workspace.

projectFolder.description: Project folder reference for organization widgets.

managedUserId.description: The managed user the widget was made for, or null when it is your own. List one managed user's widgets with the `managedUserId` or `managedUserExternalId` query parameter of `getWidgets`.

example.name: Chart Widget
example.description: Interactive chart widget for data visualization

NewWidget.description:
What a new widget starts from. Only the fields listed here are used. The widget is created without
code: it is a record with a name, a type and some starting content, on a canvas (a new one, unless you
name one of yours). It has no database: what the visitors of a composition leave is kept in the tables
of that composition.

type.description: What kind of widget this is, as a label of your choosing (for example chart, form, gallery).

content.description: Starting content for the widget. An empty object is fine.

isDraft.description: Whether the widget starts as a draft. A widget created without this is a draft.

canvasId.description: Put the widget on this existing canvas instead of a new one. You must own the canvas.

projectId.description: Project to file the widget in. You must be able to edit the project.

organizationId.description: Organization the widget belongs to. You must be a member who may create widgets there.

workspaceType.description: Whether the widget lives in your personal workspace or in an organization's.

managedUserId.description: Make the widget for one of your managed users, by Widgetic's id for the user. Send this or `managedUserExternalId`, not both. The managed user must be yours and active. The widget stays in your account; the tag lets you list one user's widgets and keeps it out of the others' lists. It is set here and does not change afterwards.

managedUserExternalId.description: The same, by your own identifier for the user, the `external_id` you gave when you created the managed user (answers show it as `externalId`). Send this or `managedUserId`, not both.

context.description: The host context the entry was stored with: what the embedding page passed in, without the two keys of a signature (`widgetic_exp` and `widgetic_sig`), which are checked when the entry comes in and are never stored.

truncatedColumns.description:
The columns whose value was cut: a value longer than 20,000 characters is cut there (a JSON value is
cut as text, so it comes back as a string and no longer as an object), and its column is named here.
Absent when nothing was cut.

nextCursor.description:
Pass it as `cursor` to get the next page. `null` on the last page, and for a table that cannot be
paged (see `paging`).

total.description:
How many entries match the filters and the `since` / `until` window, over all pages and not only this
one.

paging.description:
Present, as `unavailable`, when the table cannot be paged: it has a time column but no id column to
tell two entries of the same instant apart, or it has no time column and no id column that can be
paged on. The answer is one page only, and `nextCursor` stays `null` even when `total` is larger than
the page.

CompositionEntryAggregateTally.description:
The aggregates of one group (the entries that share a value of the `groupBy` column), or of the whole
selection when no `groupBy` was asked for. Only the functions that were asked for with `aggregate` are
present.

group.description:
The value of the `groupBy` column, as text (a number is `"5"`); `null` groups the entries that left it
empty. Absent when no `groupBy` was asked for.

count.description: How many entries are in the group (or in the selection)

avg.description:
The average of the numeric `column`, rounded to 4 decimals. `null` when no entry matched: there is no
average of nothing, and it is not 0.

min.description: The smallest value of the numeric `column`. `null` when no entry matched.

max.description: The largest value of the numeric `column`. `null` when no entry matched.

sum.description: The sum of the numeric `column`. `null` when no entry matched.

CompositionEntryAggregatesBlock.description:
What `aggregate` asked for, computed over the entries that match `since`, `until` and the `context` and
column filters of the same call.

column.description:
The numeric column `avg`, `min`, `max` and `sum` were computed over. An empty text when only `count`
was asked for.

tallies.description:
One tally per value of `groupBy`, in the order of that column (a number as a number, `null` last), up
to 200 groups; or ONE tally for the whole selection when no `groupBy` was asked for. Empty when
`groupBy` was asked for and no entry matched.

truncated.description:
True when more than 200 groups matched, so `tallies` lists the first 200 in that order. Absent
otherwise. (Not to be mixed up with `moreGroups` on the reading, which is about the plain `tallies`
of the whole table: those are 20 groups, largest first.)

values.description: Column values to insert (never id or time columns).

context.description: Host attribution from the embedding page. It is not authenticated unless the partner signs it (see the description of this operation): never use it for authorization on its own. At most 20 keys; string values up to 500 characters or finite numbers; 2048 bytes JSON total. A signed context carries two more keys, `widgetic_exp` and `widgetic_sig`: the gateway checks them and drops them, so they are neither stored nor announced.

CompositionEntryOrder.name: order
CompositionEntryOrder.description:
`desc` (the default) lists the newest entry first, `asc` the oldest. Entries are sorted by their time, then
by their id (compared as text, byte by byte) in the same direction, so the order of two entries made at the
same instant is always the same; an entry with no time counts as the oldest. A table with no time column is
sorted by its id. The managed-user feed sorts by time, then by composition id, table and id.

CompositionEntrySince.name: since
CompositionEntrySince.description:
Only entries made at this time or later: `since` is INCLUSIVE (an entry made at exactly `since` is
returned). A date and time with an offset, such as `2026-10-01T00:00:00Z`; anything else answers 400
`INVALID_SINCE`. An entry with no time never matches, and a table with no time column answers 400
`ENTRY_TABLE_HAS_NO_TIME`.

CompositionEntryUntil.name: until
CompositionEntryUntil.description:
Only entries made before this time: `until` is EXCLUSIVE (an entry made at exactly `until` is NOT
returned), so `since=A&until=B` followed by `since=B&until=C` counts every entry once. Same form and same
refusals as `since` (400 `INVALID_UNTIL`).

CompositionEntryContextFilters.name: context
CompositionEntryContextFilters.description: Host context filters as `context[key]=value` (max 5 keys, counting dotted `context.key` too). Use `column.<name>=value` for columns whose names collide with reserved parameters.

CompositionEntryColumnFilters.name: filter
CompositionEntryColumnFilters.description: Column filters as `filter[columnName]=value` (same meaning as bare `columnName=value` or `column.columnName=value`; max 10 column filters counting all spellings). A plain `filter=value` still filters a column named `filter`.

IdempotencyKeyRequired.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyRequired.description: Required: a call without it is refused with `400`. A key of your own that names this one request; a UUID is ideal. It is 8 to 50 characters of letters, digits, `-` and `_`. Send the same key again when you retry (after a timeout, a dropped connection or a `5xx`) and the call is carried out once: the retry gets the first answer back, marked `X-Idempotency-Cached: true`. The same key with a different body is refused with `422`, and a retry that arrives while the first call is still running with `409` (see `Retry-After`).

IdempotencyKeyOptional.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyOptional.description: Optional: without it the call is carried out every time it is sent. A key of your own that names this one request; a UUID is ideal. It is 8 to 50 characters of letters, digits, `-` and `_`. Send the same key again when you retry (after a timeout, a dropped connection or a `5xx`) and the call is carried out once: the retry gets the first answer back, marked `X-Idempotency-Cached: true`. The same key with a different body is refused with `422`, and a retry that arrives while the first call is still running with `409` (see `Retry-After`).
